title: Streaming-aware execution loop: result weaving, checkpoints, and recursion sentinels
text:
Streaming-aware execution loop: result weaving, checkpoints, and recursion sentinels

description:
Implement a streaming-aware tool execution loop that supports multi-tool chaining with safe result injection, incremental streaming checkpoints for partial outputs/rollbacks, and robust recursion/loop detection. This ticket covers the runtime changes, API surface for structured injection, telemetry spans for chunked streams, and compatibility shims for clients that expect synchronous tool results.

acceptance_criteria:
The executor emits streaming chunks for composite runs with a checkpoint token included in every chunk header.
Tool result injection API accepts schema descriptors and rejects incompatible results with a clear error code (TOOL_INJECTION_SCHEMA_MISMATCH).
A provenance-based recursion detector flags and halts loops with at most 0.1% false positives in unit-level tests and prevents unbounded token usage in fuzz tests.
Compatibility layer returns a synchronous aggregation endpoint that replays streaming chunks into a single final result for legacy clients.
End-to-end tests demonstrate rollback to the nearest checkpoint on tool failure and maintainable state across retries.
Telemetry includes per-tool and per-chunk latency histograms and a trace span linking request -> tool calls -> stream completion.
Documentation and SDK examples updated (Python/TS) showing streaming consumption with checkpoint resume and injection error handling.

technical_notes:
Design decision: use 'checkpoint tokens' (opaque base64 strings) returned in each stream boundary. Tokens capture minimal KV-position, last-provenance-hash, and sequence offset. This keeps tokens small and forward-compatible.
Provenance: canonicalize tool inputs+outputs and compute a SHA256 short-hash to detect repeats. Maintain a per-request Bloom filter with configurable false-positive budget to detect recursion cheaply.
Injection: require callers to attach a small JSON Schema (or pointer to model-specified schema) when invoking tool injection. The executor performs a permissive structural validation first, then stricter typed validation if schema present.
Streaming semantics: chunk metadata includes fields: checkpoint_token, provenance_hashes (last N), partiality_flag. Clients can request resume(checkpoint_token) to continue from checkpoint.
Compatibility shim: provide /v1/exec/sync-aggregate which consumes the streaming endpoint internally and returns the fully-merged output. This reduces breaking changes for existing SDK users.
Recursion policy: hard limit of 6 consecutive identical-provenance detections triggers LOOP_GUARD tripping. On trip, runtime provides a suggested mitigation payload (suggested_alternative_tools and truncation_summary).
Performance: microbenchmarks indicate ~3-5% p99 overhead for added chunk headers and provenance checks at 8k context length with batched tool calls. We'll gate via a flag and optimize kernel-path for the common case (no schema, single-tool).
Fallback: on resource constraints or Bloom filter saturation, fall back to a conservative depth-only recursion detector and mark telemetry with 'recursion_detector_fallback'.

tasks:
Spike: implement PoC checkpoint token encoding + decode library (Marco)
Runtime: integrate checkpointing into stream emission path and add resume handler (backend)
API: extend tool-invoke contract to accept optional schema pointer and error codes (API)
SDK: Python and TypeScript helpers for streaming resume+aggregate and injection errors (DX)
Tests: unit tests for Bloom filter false-positive envelope + recursion trip behavior (QA)
Load: run head-to-head p99 comparison with and without checkpointing on dedicated pool (SRE)
Docs: design doc + examples, update console docs for checkpoint tokens (PM/Docs)
PRs: open runtime and SDK PRs, coordinate staging rollout (Marco)
Security review: quick pass for schema pointer handling (sec team)
